# Purpose and scope

The A-Mab drug substance process is being transferred from `{python} SENDING_SITE` to
`{python} RECEIVING_SITE`. Stage 1 process characterization supports that transfer by
establishing which process parameters affect product quality and by defining the ranges
within which the commercial process may be operated [@fda2011]. This plan describes the
characterization study for Step `{python} f"{step_no}"` of the drug substance train, the
small virus retentive filtration step, and it is issued before any characterization data
have been generated. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor scale of
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L.

The step is the dedicated small virus removal operation of the purification train and the
principal source of MVM clearance. Its clearance is orthogonal to the two other viral
safety steps, low pH inactivation (Step 6) and anion exchange chromatography (Step 8),
because it removes virus by size rather than by inactivation or by binding [@ichq5a]. The
study covers the `{python} f"{n_params}"` process parameters of the step and the
`{python} f"{n_resp}"` responses listed in @tbl-crit. It will be executed on a qualified
scale-down model, on load material representative of the anion exchange pool that feeds
the step at commercial scale.

Three things are outside the scope of this plan. Qualification of the membrane itself is
held by the filter manufacturer and is not repeated here. The cumulative viral clearance
claim for the drug substance is consolidated across all three viral safety steps in
PCMR-001, and this study establishes only the contribution of Step
`{python} f"{step_no}"`. Process validation at commercial scale is covered by the
validation programme and not by this study.

The deliverable of the study is PCR-009, the process characterization report for this
step.

# Objectives

The study has the following objectives.

1. Qualify a scale-down model of the small virus retentive filtration step, and show that
   it represents the commercial step for virus retention, for flux decay and for step
   yield.
2. Determine which of the parameters in @tbl-params affect the two viral clearance
   responses and the step yield, in what direction and by how much.
3. Fit a response-surface model for each response over the characterization ranges, and
   establish whether it predicts the mean response adequately.
4. Derive a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each of the two viral
   clearance responses, using the criteria in §7 and the method in §8.
5. Classify each parameter under SOP-4001 and define what the step contributes to the
   control strategy and to the modular viral clearance claim.

The screening design identifies the parameters that have an effect. The response-surface
model is the predictive model, and every range claimed in PCR-009 will be derived from
it.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The step removes virus by size. The membrane carries a pore size distribution chosen to
retain the smallest viruses of concern, the parvoviruses, while the antibody passes
through. Retention is a sieving mechanism, so it depends on the integrity of the pore
structure and on how the effective pore size of the membrane changes as it fouls over the
course of a batch.

MVM sits close to the pore size cut-off, and its retention depends on the fraction of
pores at the large end of the distribution and on the flow through them. As the membrane
fouls with product and with residual impurity, flux redistributes toward the least fouled
and largest pores, and small virus can pass. MVM breakthrough therefore rises with the
volume filtered per unit area, and the highest load of a batch is the point at which
retention is weakest. A low transmembrane pressure or an interruption of flow can also allow
virus held within the pore structure to diffuse through, so pressure is controlled as well
as volume.

XMuLV is many times larger than the pores. It is retained completely while the membrane is
intact, and its clearance is insensitive to the operating parameters over any range that
can be run. Membrane integrity is confirmed after each batch by the post-use integrity
test under SOP-2012, and a membrane that passes that test has no pore large enough to pass
a retrovirus.

Step yield is limited only by product held up in the fouled membrane and in the system,
because the antibody is small enough to pass the pores freely. Yield is therefore expected
to be high and to fall slowly as the volumetric load rises.

The step is a platform operation. It has been used to manufacture three previously
licensed humanized IgG1 antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and to supply A-Mab clinical
material, with the same filter type and the same mode of operation [@amab2009]. The
mechanism of removal is size exclusion and does not depend on the identity of the
antibody, so the platform experience justifies the ranges chosen in §6.1 and supports the
expectation that MVM retention falls with volumetric load while XMuLV retention does not.
Prior knowledge does not remove the need for the study. The material presented to the
filter is the anion exchange flow-through pool of the A-Mab process, and how that pool
fouls the membrane is specific to the product, so the maximum load and the pressure range
will be established on A-Mab material.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step forms no quality attribute. It contributes log reduction to the two viral safety
attributes in @tbl-cqa, both of which are cumulative requirements on the drug substance
and are met by several steps together.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["lrv_mvm", "lrv_xmulv"]))
```

: Quality attributes the step contributes clearance to. {#tbl-cqa}

Both attributes are of very high criticality, and the risk they carry is patient safety
rather than efficacy. MVM is the harder of the two for this step. The low pH inactivation
step is not credited with any MVM clearance, because MVM is non-enveloped and low pH acts
on the lipid envelope, so the cumulative MVM requirement rests on anion exchange
chromatography and on this step alone. XMuLV is cleared by all three viral safety steps
and by the chromatography steps that make no claim, so the cumulative XMuLV requirement is
met with a wide margin.

The acceptance values in @tbl-cqa are cumulative across the process and cannot be applied
to one step. What this step must deliver is derived from them in §7.

Step yield is a process performance response. No drug substance attribute maps to it, so
it will be measured and reported but judged against no quality criterion.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 ranked the parameters of every unit operation twice, once for the potential impact
of the parameter on quality attributes and once for its potential to interact with other
parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters scoring high on either ranking were assigned to
multivariate study, parameters scoring lower were assigned to univariate study, and
parameters supported by platform knowledge alone were assigned to neither.

For this step the assessment placed `{python} f"{n_mv}"` parameters in the multivariate
group and `{python} f"{n_uv}"` in the univariate group. Filtration volume was ranked high
because MVM retention falls as the volume filtered per unit area rises, once fouling has
carried the flux onto the largest pores. Filtration pressure was ranked high because a
loss of pressure or a stop in flow lets MVM already held in the pore structure diffuse
forward into the filtrate, and because a rise in pressure drives more filtrate through the
pores that remain open. Filtration volume decides how much of the membrane is still open
and pressure decides how fast the filtrate crosses what is left, so the fall in MVM
retention with load is expected to be steeper at the top of the pressure range than at the
bottom. The designs must be able to estimate that interaction.

No parameter of this step was left out of the study on the basis of prior knowledge alone.
The risk assessment recorded that the platform claim for this step is a viral safety
claim, and that a claim of that kind should be supported by product specific data even
where the mechanism is well understood.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The study will be run on a laboratory scale filtration system fitted with the same
membrane type and the same membrane chemistry as the commercial step. The model is scaled
on membrane area, so that the volumetric load in `{python} vol.unit`, the transmembrane pressure and the
flux per unit area are the same as at commercial scale. Load material will be matched
because the product and the residual impurity the pool carries are what foul the membrane,
and a cleaner pool fouls it more slowly. Filtration temperature will be matched because a
higher temperature lowers the viscosity of the pool and raises the flux at a given
pressure. The hold-up volume per unit area will be matched because it fixes how much
product is left wetting the membrane and the tubing at the end of a run, which is what
limits the step yield.

Qualification will follow SOP-1001. Triplicate runs of the scale-down system will be
operated at the set-points in @tbl-params on representative anion exchange pool, and the
flux decay profile, the step yield and the post-use integrity test result will be compared
with the corresponding manufacturing scale records. The model will be accepted where no
statistically significant difference is found between the scales in yield or in flux decay
at the end of the load.

Virus cannot be spiked into a manufacturing batch, so every clearance figure claimed for
this step comes from the scale-down model [@ichq5a]. The weight of the claim therefore
rests on this qualification. The qualification will be repeated if the membrane type, the
filtration temperature or the composition of the load material changes, and PCR-009 will
state the qualification result before it reports any log reduction.

## Operation

The load is the flow-through pool of the anion exchange step. Each run will be operated at
constant transmembrane pressure to the volumetric load set by the design point, and the
filtrate will be collected in fractions across the load.

Before each run the filter will be wetted and its integrity tested, and after each run the
post-use integrity test will be performed, both under SOP-2012. A run whose post-use
integrity test fails will be excluded from the analysis and recorded as a deviation,
because a failed integrity test means the membrane was not intact and the log reduction
measured across it says nothing about the step.

Each design point will be executed once, with both model viruses spiked into the load
before filtration. Step yield will be determined from the same run by protein mass
balance, from the ultraviolet absorbance of the load and of the pooled filtrate. Runs will
be executed in randomized order within each design.

Filtration will be continuous. The claim made from this study applies to uninterrupted
operation, because an interruption of flow allows virus held in the pore structure to
diffuse through it. An interruption at commercial scale is a deviation and lies outside
the operating region this study will define.

## Analytical methods

Virus titre will be determined by the validated methods listed in @tbl-amv. MVM will be
titred by TCID50 with qPCR confirmation, and XMuLV by TCID50.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=VIRUS_FILT_AMV_REFS))
```

: Validated analytical methods for the viral clearance responses. {#tbl-amv}

The log reduction factor of a run is the base ten logarithm of the total virus in the
spiked load divided by the total virus in the filtrate, with both totals taken over the
volume actually filtered. Cytotoxicity and interference controls will be run for the load
matrix and the filtrate matrix, and a spike recovery control will be run for each virus
stock [@ichq5a].

Where no virus is detected in the filtrate, the titre will be reported at the limit of
detection of the assay and the log reduction reported as a lower bound rather than as a
point value. The infectivity assays carry their own variability, and the acceptance
criteria in §7 allow `{python} f"{assay_allow:g}"` log10 for it.

## Sampling plan

Samples will be taken from the load before spiking, from the spiked load, and from the
filtrate. The filtrate will be sampled as sequential fractions across the volumetric load
and as a pool at the end of the run. Fractionating the filtrate allows the log reduction
to be resolved against the volume filtered within a single run, which is the variable that
degrades MVM retention as the membrane fouls.

Each spiked load sample and each filtrate sample will be assayed for both model viruses.
The unspiked load and the unspiked filtrate pool will be assayed for protein concentration
for the yield calculation. Samples may be held frozen before assay where the method
validation supports it.

Every sample will be identified by run number and by the volumetric load at which it was
taken, and the identity will be recorded at the time of sampling.

## Statistical methods

Both factors will be coded to the interval -1 to +1 across the characterization ranges in
@tbl-params, so that the estimated effects are comparable between the two factors and
between the two designs. Effects will be reported as the change in the response over half
the characterization range.

The screening design will be analysed with a model carrying both main effects and their
interaction. The response-surface design will be analysed with the full quadratic model in
both factors. Coefficients will be reported with their standard errors and p-values, and
effects significant at α = 0.05 will be treated as real.

Model adequacy will be judged from three things. The lack of fit will be tested against
the pure error estimated from the centre point replicates. The residuals will be plotted
against the predicted value and on a normal quantile plot. The coefficient of
determination and the residual standard error will be reported for each response. The
centre point replicates also give the reproducibility of each response, which will be
reported as a coefficient of variation and used as the pure error term.

Analyses will be performed under SOP-1002. The analysis will be run from a script under
version control with a fixed random seed, so that every number in PCR-009 can be
regenerated from the raw data.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

@tbl-params lists the parameters of the step, their set-points, the ranges that will be
studied and the normal operating ranges.

```{python}
#| output: asis
```

: Parameters, characterization ranges and normal operating ranges. {#tbl-params}

Both parameters will be studied multivariately. The characterization range for the
filtration volume runs from the lower NOR edge to `{python} f"{vol.prange[1]:g}"`
`{python} vol.unit`, which lies above the upper NOR edge of
`{python} f"{vol.nor[1]:g}"` `{python} vol.unit`. The range was
widened upward only, because MVM retention falls as the volumetric load rises and holds
steady below the set-point. The edge of acceptable performance therefore lies above the NOR and
not below it, and a range extended downward would consume runs where nothing changes.

The pressure range runs from `{python} f"{pres.prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{pres.prange[1]:g}"` `{python} pres.unit` and is widened on both sides of the
NOR of `{python} f"{pres.nor[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{pres.nor[1]:g}"`
`{python} pres.unit`. Low pressures are
included because a low transmembrane pressure allows retained virus to diffuse through the
pore structure. High pressures are included because they raise the flux and compress the
fouling layer, so more filtrate passes through the largest open pores and MVM retention is
expected to fall. Both edges are reachable
by the commercial equipment, so a range that covers them supports the deviation assessment
as well as the operating limits.

@tbl-legend gives the letters used for the two factors in the design matrices of
Appendices A and B and in the effect tables of PCR-009.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
```

: Coded factor legend. {#tbl-legend}

## Screening design

The screening study will be a two-level factorial in both factors with centre point
replicates, `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs in total. `{python} f"{n_scr_f}"` runs are the
factorial points at the corners of the characterization ranges and
`{python} f"{n_scr_c}"` are replicates of the centre point.

With `{python} f"{n_fac}"` factors the full factorial is executed, so both main effects
and the interaction are estimated free of aliasing. A two-level design carries no estimate
of curvature, which is tested at the response-surface stage. The screening runs establish
the size and direction of the two effects, and the reproducibility of the infectivity
assays from the centre point replicates, before the response-surface runs are
committed.

The planned coded settings are given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study will be a face-centred central composite design in both
factors, `{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs in total. It is made up of
`{python} f"{n_rsm_f}"` factorial points, `{python} f"{n_rsm_a}"` axial points and
`{python} f"{n_rsm_c}"` centre point replicates.

The axial points sit on the edges of the characterization ranges rather than beyond them.
A rotatable design would place them outside those edges, and settings outside the ranges
in @tbl-params are not settings the step may be claimed for, so the face-centred form is
used. The design supports the full quadratic model, which allows the response to curve
against the volumetric load. Curvature is expected there, because the flux redistribution
that lets small virus through accelerates as the membrane fouls, and a model that could
only fit a straight line would over-predict retention at the top of the range.

Four replicates of the centre point give the pure error term for the lack of fit test in
§5.5 and an estimate of run to run reproducibility that does not depend on the model. The
planned coded and natural unit settings are given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

No parameter of this step is assigned to univariate study. Both parameters in @tbl-params
are factors of the two designs above, and the remaining operating variables of the step
are held at their set-points under SOP-2012 and are supported by platform experience.

Where the study finds an effect that the two designs cannot separate, a univariate
confirmation run may be added. Any such run will be justified against the data that
prompted it and reported in PCR-009 with the same acceptance criteria as the designed
runs.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

Three kinds of criterion apply to this study. One applies to the scale-down model, one to
the fitted models, and one to the responses themselves.

The scale-down model criterion is stated in §5.1. The screening runs will not begin until
it has been met, because a model that does not represent the commercial step cannot
support a viral clearance claim from it.

A fitted response-surface model will be accepted as predictive where the lack of fit test
is not significant at α = 0.05 against the pure error from the centre point replicates,
where the residuals show no trend against the predicted value and no material departure
from normality, and where the residual standard error is small against the distance
between the predicted response and its criterion. Where a model fails these checks, the
affected response will be reported descriptively and no range will be claimed from it.

@tbl-crit gives the criterion each response will be judged against.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(crit_df)
```

: Acceptance criteria for the study responses. {#tbl-crit}

The two viral clearance responses are judged against an in-process criterion rather than
against the drug substance requirement. The requirement in @tbl-cqa is cumulative, at
`{python} f"{cum_mvm:.3g}"` log10 for MVM and `{python} f"{cum_xmulv:.3g}"` log10 for
XMuLV. Subtracting the clearance credited to the other steps of the train leaves this step
a floor of `{python} f"{mvm_floor:.3g}"` log10 for MVM and
`{python} f"{xmulv_floor:.3g}"` log10 for XMuLV. The criteria in @tbl-crit are tighter
than those floors, because each is set from the log reduction credited to this step in the
modular clearance strategy, less the assay allowance of
`{python} f"{assay_allow:g}"` log10 described in §5.3. The criteria in @tbl-crit are the
tighter of the two, so the study will be judged against them, and PCR-009 will quote the
floors only to show the margin the cumulative claim retains.

Step yield carries no criterion. It will be reported with the operating region and used to
show what the region costs in product, and no acceptance decision will rest on it.

An operating range for a parameter will be declared where the response-surface model
predicts that both viral clearance responses meet their criteria across that range. The design
space for the step is the part of the characterized region where both viral clearance
responses meet their criteria at the same time, and PCR-009 will report its size from the
fitted models rather than assert that it is the whole characterized region.

Each parameter will be classified under SOP-4001 from the outcome of the study. A
parameter whose variability affects a critical quality attribute will be classified as a
CPP, or as a WC-CPP where the risk of operating outside the design space is low given the
control capability of the commercial equipment. A parameter that affects process
performance but no quality attribute will be classified as a KPP, and a parameter with
neither effect as a GPP [@ichq8].

The study will be considered successful where the scale-down model is qualified, both
viral clearance models are accepted as predictive, and a proven acceptable range
containing the NOR is established for each parameter against each of the two viral
clearance responses. Where
no such range exists, PCR-009 will report the range that does exist and the operating
limit that follows from it.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

A proven acceptable range is the range of a parameter over which the response meets its
criterion, given a stated treatment of the other parameters [@ichq8]. Two analyses will be
run for each parameter and each of the two viral clearance responses, and both will be
reported.

The first holds the other parameter at its set-point and scans the parameter of interest
across its characterization range on a grid of `{python} f"{n_par_grid}"` points, using
the fitted response-surface model. It answers what the parameter may do while the rest of
the step is operated at target.

The second varies the other parameter within its NOR by Monte-Carlo simulation of the
fitted model, with `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` draws at each of
`{python} f"{n_nor_grid}"` grid points, and takes the range over which the 95 %
prediction interval of the response stays within acceptance. The draws carry the residual
variability of the model as well as the variability of the other parameter, so this range
will normally be the narrower of the two. Where the two analyses disagree, the range from
the second is the one carried into the control strategy, because the commercial process
holds each parameter somewhere within its normal operating range and not at its
set-point.

The reported range in each case is the contiguous interval that contains the set-point.
Where the predicted response leaves acceptance inside the characterization range, the
proven acceptable range is narrower than the range studied, and PCR-009 will state the
value at which the response crosses its criterion.

Each proven acceptable range will be reported with a plot of the response against the
parameter, with the acceptance limit drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the
set-point and the NOR marked. The two analyses will be shown as the two panels of one
figure, so that the cost of the robustness criterion is visible.

The ranges themselves will be reported in PCR-009.

# Data management and integrity

Raw data will be recorded at the time of the activity, in the electronic laboratory
notebook for the process runs and in the laboratory information management system for the
analytical results. Records will meet the ALCOA+ expectations, and the audit trails of
both systems will be retained for the life of the application [@ichq10].

Analytical results will be transferred to the analysis by controlled file export. The
fitted models, the tables and the figures of PCR-009 will be generated from the exported
data by a single reproducible run of the analysis script, and a second reviewer will
confirm that the reported numbers come from that run. Any manual entry of a value into the
analysis is a data integrity finding and will be handled as one.

Deviations from this plan will be recorded when they occur and reported in PCR-009 with
their assessed impact on the study. A deviation that invalidates a design point will be
dispositioned before the affected runs are analysed, and where the disposition is to
repeat the affected runs, the superseded data will be retained and referenced rather than
deleted.

# Roles and responsibilities

@tbl-roles gives the functions involved in the study and what each is accountable for. The
named individuals are recorded in the approval table of each document rather than here, so
that a change of personnel does not require a revision of this plan.

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Process Development / MSAT | Owns this plan, executes the filtration runs, authors PCR-009 |
| Analytical Development | Performs the infectivity assays and the protein determinations under the validated methods |
| Statistics | Designs the experiments, performs the analysis, reviews model adequacy |
| Manufacturing Science, receiving site | Reviews the operating ranges against the control capability of the commercial equipment |
| Quality Assurance | Approves this plan and PCR-009, and dispositions deviations |

: Functions and responsibilities for the study. {#tbl-roles}

The receiving site reviews the ranges before they are fixed, because a range the
commercial equipment cannot hold is of no use in the control strategy [@ichq10].

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of the study is PCR-009. It will report the qualification of the
scale-down model, the screening effects, the response-surface models with their
diagnostics, the proven acceptable ranges, the design space of the step, the parameter
classification and the contribution of the step to the control strategy and to the modular
viral clearance claim.

The study will be executed in four phases, in this order.

1. Qualification of the scale-down model, against the criterion in §5.1.
2. The screening runs and their analysis.
3. The response-surface runs and their analysis.
4. The proven acceptable range analysis, the classification and the report.

Each phase begins when the preceding phase has met its criterion in §7. No calendar dates
are fixed in this plan. The study is scheduled against the transfer programme in PTP-001,
and its report rolls up into PCMR-001 with the reports of the other two viral safety
steps.

# Risks and assumptions

The clearance claim for this step rests entirely on a scale-down model, because virus
cannot be spiked at manufacturing scale. If the qualification in §5.1 fails, the study
cannot proceed. The mitigation is to re-scale the model on membrane area and on hold-up
volume and to repeat the qualification, and any change made to the model will be recorded
in PCR-009.

Spiking adds material to the load, and retention depends on how the membrane fouls. A
spike that fouls the membrane differently from unspiked process material would bias the
measured log reduction, and the bias would be largest at the top of the volumetric range,
which is the part of the range the claim depends on. The virus stock will therefore be
clarified before addition and its volume kept small against the load volume, and the flux
decay of the spiked runs will be compared with that of the unspiked qualification runs.

The log reduction that can be measured is bounded by the titre of the spiked load and by
the limit of detection of the infectivity assay. Where no virus is detected in the
filtrate, the result is a lower bound, and a lower bound that falls short of the criterion
in §7 cannot be resolved by repeating the assay. The load will therefore be spiked to a
titre that allows the criterion to be demonstrated with margin, and the achieved titre will
be reported with each run.

The study assumes that the anion exchange pool used in the runs represents commercial
material. Anion exchange is the step immediately upstream and its own characterization is
reported in PCR-008. Pool from a run that was itself out of trend will not be used, and
the load material used in each filtration run will be identified in PCR-009.

The study assumes uninterrupted filtration, as stated in §5.2. The ranges it produces do
not cover an interruption of flow, and an interruption at commercial scale will be
assessed as a deviation against the mechanism in §4.1 rather than against these ranges.

Material supply is the principal risk to the schedule. Each design point consumes anion
exchange pool, and the runs will be scheduled against pool availability rather than
against a fixed calendar.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when it has been approved by the functions listed in @tbl-appr.
Approval records that the study design in §6, the acceptance criteria in §7 and the data
management provisions in §9 are adequate to support the transfer and the viral clearance
claim.

A change to the factors, to the ranges in @tbl-params or to the acceptance criteria in
@tbl-crit after approval requires a revision of this plan and re-approval before the
affected runs are executed. A change made after the affected runs have been executed will
be reported in PCR-009 as a deviation from this plan.
